question.worked_solution:
We proceed to factor the left side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}12{y}^{3}+10{y}^{2}-6y-5 & = \\ (12{y}^{3}+10{y}^{2})-(6y+5) & = \\ 2{y}^{2}(6y+5)-(6y+5) & = \\ (6y+5)\cdot 2{y}^{2}-(6y+5)\cdot 1 & = \\ (6y+5)(2{y}^{2}-1) & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(6y+5)(2{y}^{2}-1)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(6y+5)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6y+5 & =0 \\ 6y & =-5 \\ y & =-\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $(2{y}^{2}-1)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ 2{y}^{2} & =1 \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=-\frac{5}{6},\,\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}.$
